title: The NASA Tape That Recorded Screams from Jupiter's Radiation Belt
hook: In 1992, NASA's Ulysses probe captured audio from Jupiter's magnetosphere that sounded like human screams—and they still can't explain it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines auditory horror with a real NASA mystery, triggering curiosity and unease.

title: The Asteroid That Passed So Close It Changed Earth's Rotation—In 2029
hook: Apophis will skim Earth so close in 2029 that gravity may twist our planet's spin—and trigger earthquakes.
why_this_can_go_viral: Countdown to a real event with tangible consequences, easy to visualize and fear.

title: The Declassified CIA File: 'We Tried to Teleport a Cat Using the Moon's Gravity'
hook: In 1972, the CIA allegedly attempted to exploit lunar tidal forces to teleport a test animal—the file was declassified in 2017.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd yet 'official' premise; animal testing adds dark intrigue; debunking vs. believing drives shares.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They Evolved into Immortal Data and Left the Universe
hook: What if advanced civilizations don't colonize space—they upload their minds into a simulation and vanish from the physical realm?
why_this_can_go_viral: Philosophical horror: the ultimate end of intelligence is disappearance. Sparks debate and 'what if' pondering.

title: The Anomaly That 'Split' the Moon—And Left a Perfectly Symmetrical Crack
hook: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter images show a crack across the Moon so straight it looks artificial—NASA has no explanation.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual shock: a perfect crack on the Moon challenges natural formation. Conspiracy + science combined.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Orbits' Nothing—But It's Warmer Than It Should Be
hook: A planet drifting alone in deep space radiates heat as if it has an internal furnace—something is cooking it from the inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes you question what could heat a planet in the void—radioactive decay? Alien tech? Active core?

title: The Declassified DARPA File: 'We Built a Laser That Could Vaporize Asteroids from Orbit'
hook: In the 1990s, DARPA tested a ground-based laser powerful enough to melt rock—then aimed it at a space rock.
why_this_can_go_viral: Weaponizing space: secret military programs are always viral. 'Vaporize' is a strong, visual word.

title: The Asteroid That 'Carries' a Metal Core—And It's Pulsing with Magnetism
hook: Psyche isn't just a metal asteroid—its magnetic field flickers like a heartbeat, suggesting a dormant dynamo inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: Heartbeat metaphor makes it feel alive; mystery of an active core in a dead rock holds attention.

title: The Dark Matter 'Fingerprint' That Matches No Known Particle
hook: XENON1T detected a signal that looks exactly like dark matter—but it decays in a way that defies every known physics model.
why_this_can_go_viral: A clue that contradicts all models feels like a breakthrough or a cover-up. High mystery.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came from a Cosmic Ray Burst That Sterilized the Ocean'
hook: A gamma-ray blast from 2019 may have erased 30% of marine life in the Devonian—and the same wave could hit us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Links past mass death to current danger; 'sterilized' is terrifying; creates urgency.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That 'Roams' the Galaxy—And It's Headed for the Solar System
hook: Astronomers calculated that a free-floating black hole could pass within 1 light-year of Earth in the next 100,000 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Countdown to doom; invisibility of black holes makes it even scarier; 'headed for us' triggers threat response.

title: The Declassified NSA File: 'We Received a Transmission from the Year 2042'
hook: A declassified NSA document describes intercepting a signal with a timestamp that corresponds to a date 20 years in the future.
why_this_can_go_viral: Time travel + government secrecy = viral gold. Extremely high curiosity gap. Perfect for debate.

title: The Star That 'Eats' Its Own Planets—And Then Explodes
hook: A star was observed swallowing its planets whole before going supernova—the cannibalism triggered its own death.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cannibalism is inherently shocking; the idea that a star's meal kills it is a dramatic twist.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're Trapped in a 'Gravity Well' They Can't Escape
hook: If a civilization evolves on a super-Earth with escape velocity 5x ours, they may never leave—and the universe stays silent.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes you reconsider our own luck; empathy with trapped aliens; philosophical dread.

title: The Declassified Soviet File: 'We Detected a Second Moon—And It Was Artificial'
hook: In 1966, Soviet scientists tracked a small object in lunar orbit that changed shape—their report calls it 'unidentified artificial satellite'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cold War + alien tech + declassified = perfect storm. 'Artificial' is the hook word.

title: The Asteroid That 'Carries' a Glowing Core—Visible from Earth
hook: A 2-km asteroid in the main belt emits a faint but consistent light from its center—spectroscopy reveals molten metal inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: An asteroid that glows like a tiny star—visual and mysterious. Easy to imagine and share.

title: The Dark Matter 'Hole' That Sucks Light from the Cosmic Microwave Background
hook: Astronomers found a region of the CMB that is colder than it should be—as if dark matter drained energy from the Big Bang afterglow.
why_this_can_go_viral: Suggests dark matter is actively consuming something; energy theft is a new and eerie angle.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came from a Planet That Collided with Earth—4 Billion Years Ago'
hook: The Moon-forming impact nearly vaporized Earth—but recent evidence suggests the colliding planet left a dark remnant inside us.
why_this_can_go_viral: An 'alien planet inside Earth' is a stunning concept; ties to our own origin and hidden danger.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Eats' Its Own Atmosphere—Then Collapses
hook: A lonely gas giant is slowly consuming its own atmosphere from the inside out—its core is collapsing into a black dwarf.
why_this_can_go_viral: Suicidal planet is a compelling metaphor; 'eating itself' is grotesque and unforgettable.

title: The Declassified DARPA File: 'We Tested a Nuclear Warhead on a Meteor—And It Survived'
hook: In 1960s, DARPA detonated a nuke on a space rock to test deflection—the rock didn't break. It just kept coming.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nuke + asteroid + failure = irresistible. Underscores our vulnerability; government testing gone wrong.
